statutory_reference: Drugs and Cosmetics Rules 1945, Rule 122-E & New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules 2019
description: Application for permission to conduct Clinical Trials and manufacture/import a Phytopharmaceutical Drug (defined as purified and standardized fraction with minimum 4 bioactive markers of botanical origin).
mandatory_dossier_requirements: Botanical identification, geographical origin, and herbarium voucher specimen documentation
Chromatographic fingerprinting (HPLC / HPTLC / LC-MS) with quantified minimum 4 bioactive phytochemical markers
Heavy metal limits compliance (Lead < 10 ppm, Arsenic < 3 ppm, Cadmium < 0.3 ppm, Mercury < 1 ppm)
Pesticide residue testing (EPA / European Pharmacopoeia limits) and Aflatoxin testing (B1 < 2 ppb, Total < 4 ppb)
Non-clinical safety: Acute oral toxicity, 28-day sub-acute toxicity, Ames mutagenicity test
Phase I, Phase II, and Phase III clinical trial protocol approved by registered Institutional Ethics Committee (IEC)
Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) certificate of manufacturing premises
fee_structure_inr: INR 50,000 for clinical trial permission; INR 2,00,000 for new phytopharmaceutical drug manufacturing permission.
average_timeline_days: 90 to 180 days for CDSCO Subject Expert Committee (SEC) review.

portal: State AYUSH e-Aushadhi / State Licensing Authority Portal
description: License to manufacture Proprietary Ayurvedic Medicines whose ingredients are all listed in First Schedule classical texts, with traditional indications and standard dosage forms.
mandatory_dossier_requirements: Formulation composition with Sanskrit and botanical names of all raw ingredients
Exact citations from First Schedule authoritative texts establishing traditional medicinal use
Acute oral toxicity data (OECD Guideline 423) demonstrating safety in animal models
Batch Manufacturing Record (BMR) and shelf-life stability test protocol (minimum 3 years)
Schedule 'T' GMP compliance certificate for premises, water treatment, and machinery
Bio-data and appointment letter of full-time qualified Ayurvedic physician and analytical chemist
fee_structure_inr: INR 1,000 to INR 3,000 per product formulation depending on the State AYUSH authority.

portal: State AYUSH Licensing Authority Portal with Expert Technical Committee
description: License for Proprietary Ayurvedic Medicines using classical ingredients but claiming a new therapeutic indication, modified dosage route (e.g. sublingual nano-drops), or altered ratio of components.
mandatory_dossier_requirements: Full pharmacological rationale for the modification or new indication
Pilot Clinical Trial Report conducted on at least 30 patients under the supervision of a qualified MD (Ayurveda) physician or hospital
Acute and sub-acute (28-day) animal toxicity study reports from an approved testing laboratory
Accelerated and real-time stability testing data (minimum 6 months accelerated)
Proof of heavy metal, aflatoxin, microbial, and pesticide residue compliance
Schedule 'T' GMP certified manufacturing facility
fee_structure_inr: INR 5,000 to INR 10,000 per product formulation + clinical protocol inspection fees.

statutory_reference: Drugs and Cosmetics Act 1940, Section 3(a) & Rule 158-B
description: Manufacturing license for traditional classical formulations directly matching recipes in authoritative books listed in the First Schedule (Charaka Samhita, Sushruta Samhita, Sharangadhara, etc.).
mandatory_dossier_requirements: Exact name and shloka/verse citation of the classical scripture where the recipe is documented
Undertaking that no alteration has been made to the formulation ratio, processing method, or excipients
COMPLETELY EXEMPT from clinical trials and animal safety studies (legal presumption of safety)
Schedule 'T' GMP compliance of premises, raw herb authenticity testing, and finished product quality specs
fee_structure_inr: INR 500 to INR 2,000 per classical formulation.

statutory_reference: Drugs and Cosmetics Act 1940, Section 3(aaa) & Cosmetic Rules
description: License to manufacture Ayurvedic cosmetics (Saundarya Prasadak) intended for external cleansing, beautification, or skin/hair vitality.
mandatory_dossier_requirements: List of herbal ingredients with extraction methods and certificates of analysis (CoA)
Compliance with Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) specifications for skin irritation, patch test, and ocular irritation
Heavy metals safety report (Lead < 20 ppm, Arsenic < 2 ppm, Mercury < 1 ppm)
Draft label layout strictly free from medicinal/disease cure claims
Qualified Ayurvedic or cosmetic chemist supervision proof
fee_structure_inr: INR 2,500 for license fee + INR 1,000 inspection fee.

portal: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FOSCOS - foscos.fssai.gov.in)
form_name: FSSAI Central Food Business Operator (FBO) License
statutory_reference: Food Safety and Standards (Ayurveda Aahar) Regulations, 2022
description: Mandatory central license for foods prepared in accordance with Ayurvedic recipes for nutritional support, dietary supplementation, and physiological harmony.
mandatory_dossier_requirements: Evidence that all ingredients are documented in authoritative Ayurvedic texts (Schedule I books)
Strict declaration that the product is NOT for parenteral or injectable administration
Packaging layout displaying the official registered 'Ayurveda Aahar' logo on the principal display panel
Mandatory disclaimer: 'NOT FOR MEDICINAL USE - To be used as a dietary supplement only'
FSSAI Food Safety Plan, water test report, and food handler medical fitness certificates
fee_structure_inr: INR 7,500 per year for Central FSSAI License.

form_name: NBA Form I (Access to Biological Resources / TK)
statutory_reference: Biological Diversity Act 2002, Section 3 & BD Rules 2024 Rule 14
description: Mandatory statutory application for non-Indian entities, NRIs, foreign citizens, or Indian companies with any foreign shareholding to access Indian biological resources or associated traditional knowledge for commercial utilization or research.
mandatory_dossier_requirements: Detailed description of biological resource (botanical name, plant parts, quantity required)
Geographical location of harvest/collection and proof of local BMC (Biodiversity Management Committee) consultation
Executive summary of proposed commercial project, manufacturing process, and target markets
Benefit Sharing Agreement commitment: Undertaking to share 0.1% to 0.5% of ex-factory sales or 3.0% to 5.0% of purchase price with NBA
Criminal penalty warning: Accessing Indian biological resources without Form I approval is punishable with imprisonment up to 5 years and fines under Section 55
fee_structure_inr: INR 10,000 application fee payable to National Biodiversity Authority, Chennai.

form_name: NBA Form III (Application for IPR / Patent Approval)
statutory_reference: Biological Diversity Act 2002, Section 6 & BD Rules 2024 Rule 18
description: Mandatory statutory approval required before applying for or sealing ANY Intellectual Property Right (patent) in India or outside India based on biological resources or traditional knowledge obtained from India.
mandatory_dossier_requirements: Copy of patent application, patent specification, and claims filed or intended to be filed
Exact source and geographical origin of biological resources used in the patent specification
Declaration whether the patent applicant is an Indian citizen, Indian entity, or foreign entity
Benefit sharing proposal for commercial exploitation of the patent (0.2% to 1.0% royalty on sales)
Mandatory requirement: Indian Patent Office (IPO) will NOT grant a patent without Form III clearance under Section 6
fee_structure_inr: INR 500 for Indian individual / MSME; INR 10,000 for large entities / foreign applicants.
